]]> Archer Aviation partners with Walt Disney Imagineering to explore the future of air travel https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/news/archer-aviation-walt-disney-future-of-flight/ Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:28:50 +0000 https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/?p=57518 Archer Aviation and Walt Disney Imagineering are joining forces to explore the future of flight, linking next-generation eVTOL aircraft with Disney's expertise in immersive experiences and innovation.

The post Archer Aviation partners with Walt Disney Imagineering to explore the future of air travel appeared first on AGN.

]]> Archer Aviation has teamed up with the research and development (R&D) arm of Walt Disney Imagineering to begin early, exploratory research into the future of transportation.

The electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) developer unveiled the collaboration on 19 November, when its Midnight aircraft appeared at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix in a custom Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Doomsday and Disney branded livery.

Walt Disney Imagineering R&D and Archer Aviation are beginning early, exploratory research together on the future of transportation. An Avengers: Doomsday eVTOL is the first sign of a new partnership ⬇️ 🔗 https://t.co/n7J7nT3Ge5 https://t.co/M2Gs6NVBkn

— BlogMickey.com (@Blog_Mickey) November 20, 2026

The reveal comes just ahead of the film’s cinema release on 18 December. Showing the aircraft at one of the world’s most recognisable sporting and entertainment events was a deliberate move and builds on Archer’s earlier announcement on 12 November of a global air taxi partnership with Formula 1.

Read more about how Formula 1 could introduce flying taxis at Grand Prix races in Archer deal Read more about how Formula 1 could introduce flying taxis at Grand Prix races in Archer deal

Archer’s remit for the Disney collaboration is deliberately broad

According to Archer, the collaboration brings together aviation, storytelling and innovation, with the two companies planning to explore what may be possible in the future through creative, technical and experiential concepts. That wording leaves the scope open, with no specific products or timelines announced yet. Nonetheless, it is notable that Walt Disney Imagineering R&D wants to attach its name to Archer and research into how people might travel in the future.

In a LinkedIn post, Adam Goldstein, Founder and CEO of Archer, said: “Imagination has always pushed aviation forward, and this collaboration with the Walt Disney Company is no different.”

Why Archer’s partnership with Walt Disney Imagineering matters

For Archer, the benefits are as much about public perception as engineering. Air taxis face a persistent challenge: being accepted by people and persuading them that eVTOL travel is exciting, safe, and could be part of everyday life. Few organisations are better placed to shape that narrative than Disney, with its reputation for bringing characters, technology and fantasy worlds to life by building emotional connections with audiences.

Archer joins a growing list of technology companies – including Adobe, NVIDIA and Adobe – that are increasingly turning to Disney to help shape the future of storytelling. Kyle Laughlin, SVO, Walt Disney Imagineering R&D, explains the company has always described its “product as emotion,” adding that these collaborations bring stories to life in meaningful ways and “help us make that connection even faster.”

Imagineering described as both a world-class design firm and cutting-edge innovation lab, brings a team of passionate individuals with a shared goal of pushing boundaries, thinking big and embracing creativity.

Archer builds partnerships to grow its presence

The partnership with Walt Disney Imagineering also helps Archer keep its profile in the spotlight as it moves towards commercial operations and builds on other recent collaborations.

Midnight, Archer’s piloted four-passenger eVTOL, is designed for short urban hops. It could shorten journeys that currently take 60 to 90 minutes by road to flights lasting between 10 and 20 minutes. Archer has partnered with various industry stakeholders in the last year, most recently with ITA Airways on an electric air taxi network in Italy. Other airline partners include United Airlines, Southwest Air, Japan Airways, Korean Air and Ethiopian Airlines.

The eVTOL developer also recently conducted several days of piloted flight demonstrations in California’s San Francisco Bay area and has been building a public presence through high-profile events and partnerships, including its tie-up with Formula 1.

What comes next?

Because the collaboration with Disney is exploratory, tangible outcomes may be some way off. For now, the partnership signals that Archer wants to be seen as integral to the wider cultural conversation about how we will travel in the future. Whether that results in new passenger experiences, themed flights, or something entirely different remains to be seen.

]]> Why is Google buying data from bankrupt Spirit Airlines? https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/news/google-spirit-airlines-data-sale/ Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:11:14 +0000 https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/?p=57508 A US bankruptcy judge approved Google’s $10 million purchase of Spirit Airlines records. Google plans to use the data for product development and AI training.

The post Why is Google buying data from bankrupt Spirit Airlines? appeared first on AGN.

]]> A US bankruptcy judge has approved Google’s $10 million purchase of internal business records from Spirit Airlines. Google says it will use the material for product development and to train artificial intelligence models.

Judge Sean Lane approved the sale on 17 November, Reuters reported, after Google agreed to tighter safeguards for former employees’ data. The sale covers material from emails, spreadsheets and calendars, as well as records relating to marketing, productivity and airline operations.

Spirit ceased flying on 2 May after talks over a government bailout collapsed. The ultra-low-cost carrier had returned to Chapter 11 in August 2025, hoping to recover through a reorganisation that included a substantial fleet reduction. 

The recovery was unsuccessful and, as Spirit wound down, its bankruptcy estate put the records up for auction. Google won the bidding in August with a $10 million offer. AI company Mercor was named the alternate bidder at $7.5 million, according to a bankruptcy court filing.

What does Google want with airline records?

Google’s plans for the records, reported by Reuters in August, are to use them as examples of how work moves between common business tools. The reporting did not identify which Google products or models would use the material.

An email can provide the context for a decision, a calendar can show when a team discussed it, and a spreadsheet can record the figures behind it. A dataset that keeps those connections intact can provide examples for training an AI model to bring together information scattered across different files, such as when answering a question about a project.

What happens to passenger and employee data?

The connections raised privacy concerns. As AGN reported in August, the flight attendants’ union challenged the proposed sale over the range of employee material potentially in scope. In its initial objection, the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA highlighted a provision in the original agreement that called for links between records to be preserved during de-identification. 

“Worker data privacy in the age of AI has become a whole new worker’s rights issue,” said Sara Nelson, international president of the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA.

In an October letter, 121 US lawmakers warned that removing direct identifiers such as names and email addresses could still leave clues that allow information to be traced back to individuals.

Reuters reported that the consumer privacy ombudsman recommended approval in October after excluding personal information relating to 97 million Spirit customers from the transaction.

Under the revised terms, the flight attendants’ union said health and medical information, drug and alcohol testing records, disciplinary files, safety programme records and identification documents are excluded.

Data going to Google must undergo de-identification under the ISO/IEC 27559 international standard. An independent agent chosen in consultation with the unions will check the results. 

Google must handle the records in a secure environment and keep them confidential. The terms also bar Google from attempting to identify individuals in the dataset, the union said.

In a filing withdrawing objections on the day of the hearing, the union said the withdrawal would take effect once the court entered a written order substantially in the form negotiated with Spirit and Google.

 }

.sie-hdr__has-dropdown.is-open > .sie-hdr__dropdown {
 display: block;
}
.sie-hdr__dropdown li {
 margin: 0;
 padding: 0;
}
.sie-hdr__dropdown a {
 display: block;
 padding: 10px 18px;
 font-size: 13.5px;
 color: #003B73;
 font-weight: 500;
 border-radius: 0;
 min-height: unset;
}
.sie-hdr__dropdown a:hover {
 background: #f0f7ff;
 color: #0b5394;
}
.sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle svg {
 transition: transform 0.2s ease;
}
.sie-hdr__has-dropdown.is-open .sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle svg,
.sie-hdr__has-dropdown:hover .sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle svg {
 transform: rotate(180deg);
}
/* ── Mobile hamburger ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr__hamburger {
 display: none;
 flex-direction: column;
 justify-content: center;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 5px;
 width: 44px;
 height: 44px;
 background: none;
 border: none;
 cursor: pointer;
 padding: 0;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 margin-left: auto;
}
.sie-hdr__hamburger span {
 display: block;
 width: 22px;
 height: 2px;
 background: #fff;
 border-radius: 2px;
 transition: transform 0.25s ease, opacity 0.25s ease;
}
/* Animate to ✕ when open */
.sie-hdr__hamburger[aria-expanded="true"] span:nth-child(1) {
 transform: translateY(7px) rotate(45deg);
}
.sie-hdr__hamburger[aria-expanded="true"] span:nth-child(2) {
 opacity: 0;
}
.sie-hdr__hamburger[aria-expanded="true"] span:nth-child(3) {
 transform: translateY(-7px) rotate(-45deg);
}
/* ── User-UI icon bar integration ────────────────────────────────────────────
 user-ui.php's desktop bar uses position:absolute; top:20px; right:30px — that
 was designed for Divi's header context. Inside our flex .sie-hdr__inner we
 need it as a normal flex child instead.
 Fixed-position children (auth drawer, mobile bar, destinations panel) are
 unaffected — position:fixed is always viewport-relative provided no ancestor

@media (max-width: 860px) {

.sie-hdr .se-ai-icon {

 height: 36px !important;

}
/* Icon colours inside the header.

.sie-hdr .se-shortlist-link,
.sie-hdr .se-dest-desktop-btn,
.sie-hdr .se-user-icon {

.sie-hdr .se-shortlist-link:hover,
.sie-hdr .se-dest-desktop-btn:hover,
.sie-hdr .se-user-icon:hover {

}

.sie-hdr .se-fav-desktop-link {

}
.sie-hdr .se-fav-desktop-link:hover {

}

@media (max-width: 860px) {

 inset: 0;

.sie-field-hero{position: relative; 
 left: 50%;
 right: 50%;
 margin-left: -50vw;
 margin-right: -50vw;
 width: 100vw; 
 min-height: 480px;
 max-height: 560px;
 background-size: cover;
 background-position: center 40%;
 background-repeat: no-repeat; 
 background-color: #003B73;
 overflow: hidden;
 margin-bottom: 0;}
.sie-field-hero--no-image{background: linear-gradient(
 135deg,
 var(--field-color, #003B73) 0%,
 color-mix(in srgb, var(--field-color, #003B73) 65%, #000) 100%
 );}
.sie-field-hero__bg-img{position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 width: 100%;
 height: 100%;
 object-fit: cover;
 object-position: center 40%;
 z-index: 0;
 display: block;}
.sie-field-hero__overlay{position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 z-index: 1;
 background: linear-gradient(
 to top,
 rgba(0, 20, 50, 0.90) 0%,
 rgba(0, 20, 50, 0.60) 38%,
 rgba(0, 20, 50, 0.25) 65%,
 rgba(0, 20, 50, 0.12) 100%
 );
 display: flex;
 align-items: flex-end;
 padding-bottom: 52px;}
.sie-field-hero__inner{width: 100%;
 max-width: 1100px;
 margin: 0 auto;
 padding: 0 32px;}
.sie-field-hero__label{display: block;
 font-size: 13px;
 font-weight: 500;
 color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.75);
 margin-bottom: 12px;
 letter-spacing: 0.03em;}
.sie-field-hero__label a{color: inherit;
 text-decoration: none;}
.sie-field-hero__label a:hover{color: #fff;
 text-decoration: underline;}
.sie-field-category-badge{display: inline-flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 7px;
 padding: 6px 14px;
 background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.18);
 border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35);
 color: #fff;
 font-size: 12px;
 font-weight: 600;
 border-radius: 20px;
 margin-bottom: 14px;
 backdrop-filter: blur(8px);
 -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(8px);
 letter-spacing: 0.03em;}
.sie-field-category-badge i{font-size: 11px;
 opacity: 0.9;}
.sie-field-hero__title{font-size: clamp(30px, 5vw, 54px);
 font-weight: 800;
 color: #ffffff;
 margin: 0 0 14px;
 line-height: 1.1;
 letter-spacing: -0.02em;
 max-width: auto;}
.sie-field-hero__tagline{font-size: clamp(15px, 2vw, 18px);
 color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88);
 margin: 0 0 28px;
 max-width: auto;
 line-height: 1.55;
 font-weight: 400;}
.sie-field-hero__actions{display: flex;
 flex-wrap: wrap;
 gap: 12px;
 margin-top: 4px;}
.sie-field-hero__cta{display: inline-flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 8px;
 padding: 12px 24px;
 background: #1E56B0;
 color: #fff;
 font-size: 14px;
 font-weight: 600;
 border-radius: 6px;
 text-decoration: none;
 transition: background 0.2s;
 white-space: nowrap;}
.sie-field-hero__cta:hover{background: #163e82;
 color: #fff;
 text-decoration: none;}
.sie-field-hero__cta--secondary{background: transparent;
 border: 2px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.6);}
.sie-field-hero__cta--secondary:hover{background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12);
 border-color: #fff;}
.sie-field-body{max-width: 1200px;
 margin: 0 auto;
 padding: 0 24px 80px;}
.sie-field-highlights{display: flex;
 flex-wrap: wrap;
 gap: 0;
 background: #f0f4fb;
 border: 1px solid #d4e0f5;
 border-radius: 12px;
 margin: 32px 0 40px;
 overflow: hidden;}
.sie-field-intro-block{margin: 0 0 48px;}
.sie-field-intro-block p{font-size: 17px;
 line-height: 1.78;
 color: #374151;
 margin: 0;

 .lh-page-h1 is the homepage's monospaced eyebrow and keeps its own face. */
main h1:not(.lh-page-h1),main h2,#main-content h1:not(.lh-page-h1),#main-content h2{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;letter-spacing:-.3px}
/* ── Program search + results (2026-11-09) ─────────────────────────────────
 Shared by /search, the /in-english finder panel, the homepage hero and
 Leonardo's results, so one set of rules brings all of them along: navy
 actions, hairline cards, neutral tags. The country colours of the flow view
 arrive as inline custom properties, hence the !important. */
.sie-sps-bar{border:1px solid #C3C9CE !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-sps-bar:focus-within{border-color:#12233D !important;box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(18,35,61,.10) !important}
.sie-sps-btn{background:#12233D !important;color:#fff !important;border-color:#12233D !important;border-radius:4px !important;font-weight:600 !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-sps-btn:hover{background:#1E3354 !important}
.sie-ai-switch input:checked + .sie-ai-slider{background:#12233D !important}
.sie-results-dock{border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:8px !important;box-shadow:0 2px 10px rgba(18,35,61,.08) !important}
.sie-filter-badge.active{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important;border:1px solid #C3C9CE !important}
.sie-finder-overlay__head--branded{background:#12233D !important}
.sie-flow__branch{--branch-color:#12233D !important;--branch-bg:#F4F2ED !important;border-color:#E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-flow__source-pill,.sie-flow__junction-dot{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important}
.sie-flow__source-pill{border-radius:4px !important}
.sie-flow__prog{border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-flow__prog--partner{border-left:3px solid #12233D !important}
.sie-flow__prog--partner{outline:none !important}
.sie-flow__card-front,.sie-flow__card-back,.program-card{border-radius:6px !important}
.sie-flow__prog-tag{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#3C4F66 !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:3px !important}
.sie-flow__prog-tag i{color:#6B6456 !important}
.sie-lead-button.sie-cta-button,.sie-flow__visit-link{background:#12233D !important;color:#fff !important;border-radius:4px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-lead-button.sie-cta-button:hover,.sie-flow__visit-link:hover{background:#1E3354 !important}
.sie-flow__expand-btn i{color:#12233D !important}
.sie-verified-badge{background:#F4F2ED !important;border-color:#E4E0D8 !important;color:#3C4F66 !important;border-radius:3px !important}
.sie-verified-badge i{color:#1C7A4A !important}
/* ── Search results panel: header, filters, "At a glance" (2026-11-10) ───── */
.sie-results-dock{background:#fff !important;color:#1F2A37 !important}
.sie-dock-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;font-size:21px !important;color:#12233D !important;letter-spacing:-.01em}
.sie-dock-sub img{display:none !important}
.sie-dock-sub .sub-txt{color:#4A525C !important;opacity:1 !important;font-size:14px !important}
.sie-dock-sub .sub-txt strong{color:#12233D}
.sie-dock-close{color:#12233D !important}
.sie-filter-toggle,.sie-filter-pill,.sie-size-btn,.sie-reset-btn{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border:1px solid #C3C9CE !important;border-radius:4px !important;box-shadow:none !important;font-family:inherit !important;font-weight:600 !important}
.sie-filter-toggle:hover,.sie-filter-pill:hover,.sie-size-btn:hover{border-color:#12233D !important}
.sie-size-btn.active{background:#12233D !important;border-color:#12233D !important;color:#fff !important}
.sie-reset-btn{border-style:dashed !important}
.sie-filter-badge{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important;border:1px solid #C3C9CE !important;border-radius:3px !important;font-weight:600 !important}
.sie-ctrl-label{font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace !important;font-size:11px !important;font-weight:500 !important;letter-spacing:.08em !important;text-transform:uppercase !important;color:#6B6456 !important}
.sie-popover{border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(18,35,61,.12) !important}
.sie-pop-head{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;color:#12233D !important}
.sie-pop-search{border:1px solid #C3C9CE !important;border-radius:4px !important}
.sie-chip{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border:1px solid #D5D0C6 !important;border-radius:4px !important;font-family:inherit !important;font-weight:600 !important}
.sie-chip.active{background:#12233D !important;border-color:#12233D !important;color:#fff !important}
/* At a glance */
.sie-ovv{border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-ovv__head{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;font-size:18px !important;color:#12233D !important}
.sie-ovv__bar{border-radius:2px !important;overflow:hidden}
.sie-ovv__bar > *{background:#12233D !important;border-right:2px solid #fff}
.sie-ovv__bar > *:nth-child(2){background:#3C4F66 !important}
.sie-ovv__bar > *:nth-child(3){background:#6B7A8F !important}

.sie-ovv__lbl{font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace !important;font-weight:500 !important;letter-spacing:.08em !important;color:#6B6456 !important}
.sie-ovv__chip{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border:1px solid #D5D0C6 !important;border-radius:4px !important;font-family:inherit !important;font-weight:600 !important}
.sie-ovv__chip i{color:#8C5A23 !important}
.sie-ovv__chip:hover{border-color:#12233D !important}
.sie-ovv__chip.is-active{background:#12233D !important;border-color:#12233D !important;color:#fff !important}
.sie-ovv__chip.is-active i{color:#fff !important}
.sie-ovv__basis-btn{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;font-family:inherit !important;font-weight:600 !important}
.sie-ovv__basis-btn.is-on{background:#12233D !important;color:#fff !important}
.sie-ovv__basis{border:1px solid #C3C9CE !important;border-radius:4px !important;overflow:hidden}
/* Flow area and card names */
#sie-flow-view-container{background:#FAF8F4 !important;border-radius:6px}
.sie-flow__summary{color:#4A525C !important}
.sie-flow__source-pill{box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-flow__branch-icon{border-radius:4px !important}
.sie-flow__branch-count{border-radius:3px !important;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace !important;font-weight:500 !important}
.sie-flow__branch-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;color:#12233D !important}

/* ── Study-fields block, everywhere it appears (was homepage-only via page-id-150) ── */
body .sie-fields-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.4px;color:#12233D}
body .sie-fields-subtitle{color:#4A525C}
body .sie-fields-flow__source-pill{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;box-shadow:none !important;border-radius:4px !important}
body .sie-fields-flow__junction-dot{background:#12233D !important}
body .sie-fields-flow__branch{--branch-color:#12233D !important;--branch-bg:#F4F2ED !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
body .sie-fields-flow__branch-accent{display:none !important}
body .sie-fields-flow__branch-icon{background:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px !important}
body .sie-fields-flow__branch-count{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important}
body .sie-fields-flow__field-card{background:#FAF8F4 !important;border:1px solid #EDEAE3 !important;border-radius:5px !important}

body .sie-fields-flow__field-icon{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px !important}
body .sie-fields-flow__leo-link{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
body .sie-fields-leonardo{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;border-radius:6px !important}
body .sie-fields-leo-btn{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border-color:#fff !important;border-radius:4px !important}
/* ── Study Destinations sliding panel ── */
.sie-dest-panel__backdrop{background:rgba(18,35,61,.45) !important;-webkit-backdrop-filter:none !important;backdrop-filter:none !important}
.sie-dest-panel__sheet{background:#FAF8F4 !important;border-left:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;box-shadow:-12px 0 32px rgba(18,35,61,.18) !important;padding:34px 32px 40px !important}
.sie-dest-panel__globe{display:none !important}
.sie-dest-panel__title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;color:#12233D !important;font-size:28px !important;letter-spacing:-.01em !important}
.sie-dest-panel__sub{color:#4A525C !important}
.sie-dest-panel__close{border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;background:#fff !important;color:#4A525C !important;border-radius:4px !important}

.sie-dest-hero{background-color:#12233D !important}
.sie-dest-hero--no-image{background:#12233D !important}
.sie-dest-hero__overlay{background:linear-gradient(to top,rgba(18,35,61,.92) 0%,rgba(18,35,61,.62) 42%,rgba(18,35,61,.28) 72%,rgba(18,35,61,.12) 100%) !important}
.sie-dest-hero[class*="sie-flag-"]::after{width:6px !important;opacity:.95 !important}

.sie-dest-hero__cta{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border-radius:4px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-dest-hero__cta i{color:#12233D !important}
.sie-dest-hero__cta:hover{background:#F4F2ED !important}
.sie-country-heart--hero{border-radius:4px !important;background:transparent !important;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.45) !important;color:#fff !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-finder-bar{border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-finder-bar__count{color:#12233D !important;font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important}
.sie-finder-bar__browse{background:#12233D !important;border-radius:4px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-finder-pill{border-radius:4px !important;background:#fff !important;border:1px solid #D5D0C6 !important;color:#12233D !important}
.sie-finder-pill:hover{border-color:#12233D !important}
.sie-dest-stats{background:#fff !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-dest-stat__label{font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace !important;letter-spacing:.06em !important;color:#6B6456 !important}
.sie-dest-stat__value{color:#12233D !important;font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important}
.sie-dest-section h2{color:#12233D !important}
.sie-dest-section__subhead{color:#6B6456 !important}
.sie-dest-signal{background:#fff !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-left:3px solid #1C7A4A !important;border-radius:4px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-dest-signal i{color:#1C7A4A !important}
.sie-dest-section--signals_warn .sie-dest-signal{border-left-color:#B7791F !important}
.sie-dest-section--signals_warn .sie-dest-signal i{color:#B7791F !important}
.sie-dest-card{background:#fff !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-dest-card__title{color:#12233D !important}
.sie-dest-table th{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important}
.sie-dest-table th,.sie-dest-table td{border-color:#E4E0D8 !important}
.sie-dest-country-card{background:#fff !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-dest-country-card__name{color:#12233D !important;font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important}
.sie-dest-field-child{background:#fff !important;background-image:none !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-top:3px solid var(--field-accent,#12233D) !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important;color:#12233D !important}

.sie-dest-field-child__icon{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px !important}
.sie-dest-field-child__title,.sie-dest-field-child i{color:#12233D !important}
.sie-dest-guide-card{background:#fff !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-top:3px solid #12233D !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-dest-guide-card__icon{background:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px !important}
.sie-dest-guide-card__cta{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
.sie-dest-leonardo{background:#F4F2ED !important;background-image:none !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:8px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-dest-leonardo .sie-leo-avatar{display:none !important}
.sie-dest-leonardo p{color:#4A525C !important}
.sie-dest-leonardo .sie-field-prompt-label{color:#6B6456 !important}
.sie-dest-leonardo .sie-field-leonardo-chat{border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.sie-dest-leonardo .sie-field-prompt-btn{background:#fff !important;border:1px solid #D5D0C6 !important;border-radius:4px !important;color:#12233D !important;font-family:inherit !important}
.sie-dest-leonardo .sie-field-chat-input{border:1px solid #C3C9CE !important;border-radius:4px !important}
.sie-dest-leonardo .sie-field-chat-submit{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;border-radius:4px !important;box-shadow:none !important}

#se-mobile-bottom-bar{background:rgba(250,248,244,.97) !important;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important}
#se-mobile-bottom-bar .se-toggle-bar{background:#12233D !important}
#se-mobile-bottom-bar .se-toggle-bar i{color:#fff !important}
#se-mobile-bottom-bar .se-pill-btn{background:#fff !important;background-image:none !important;color:#12233D !important;border:1px solid #D5D0C6 !important;border-radius:4px !important;box-shadow:none !important;font-weight:600 !important}
#se-mobile-bottom-bar .se-pill-btn i{color:#6B6456 !important}

/* ── Resources pages (2026-11-09) ── */
/* Breadcrumb (Breadcrumb plugin, theme2): plain text trail instead of boxed links. */
.breadcrumb-container ol{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;list-style:none;margin:0 0 14px !important;padding:0 !important}
.breadcrumb-container li{display:inline-flex;align-items:center}
.breadcrumb-container li a{background:none !important;border:0 !important;box-shadow:none !important;padding:4px 0 !important;margin:0 !important;border-radius:0 !important;font-size:13px;color:#4A525C !important}
.breadcrumb-container li a span{color:inherit !important}
.breadcrumb-container li a:hover{color:#12233D !important;text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:3px}
.breadcrumb-container li:last-child a{color:#12233D !important;font-weight:600}
.breadcrumb-container li:not(:last-child)::after{content:"\203A";margin:0 9px;color:#9A958A;font-size:14px}
.breadcrumb-container .separator{display:none !important}
/* Full-width pages (e.g. /in-english) print the trail in a bare<nav>; give it the content column. */
nav > .breadcrumb-container{max-width:1080px;margin:0 auto;padding:14px 24px 0;box-sizing:border-box}
/* Grades + Tuition fees: no glowing orbs, no gradients, navy calls to action. */
.gr-orb,.tuition-orb{display:none !important}
.gr-universe,.tuition-universe{background:#F4F2ED !important;background-image:none !important;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-bottom:1px solid #E4E0D8}
.gr-card-header,.tuition-card-header{background:#F4F2ED !important;background-image:none !important;border-bottom:1px solid #E4E0D8}
.gr-ects-inner,.sie-content details{background:#fff !important;background-image:none !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.gr-leo-cta-inner,.leo-tuition-cta-inner{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.gr-leo-cta-btn,.leo-tuition-cta-btn{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border:1px solid #fff !important;border-radius:4px !important;font-weight:600 !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.gr-leo-cta-btn:hover,.leo-tuition-cta-btn:hover{background:#F4F2ED !important}
.tuition-card-leo{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important}
/* Grade bands keep their meaning (A best → F fail) as a thin coloured rule on a
 neutral row, instead of five pastel fills. */
.gr-grade{background:#FAF8F4 !important;border-left:3px solid #C3C9CE;border-radius:3px !important}
.gr-grade-a{border-left-color:#4F8A62 !important}.gr-grade-b{border-left-color:#86A05A !important}.gr-grade-c{border-left-color:#C2A243 !important}.gr-grade-d{border-left-color:#C7843F !important}.gr-grade-f{border-left-color:#B0554B !important}
.gr-ects-pill{background:#FAF8F4 !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-left-width:3px !important;color:#12233D !important;border-radius:3px !important}
.gr-ects-a{border-left-color:#4F8A62 !important}.gr-ects-b{border-left-color:#86A05A !important}.gr-ects-c{border-left-color:#C2A243 !important}.gr-ects-d{border-left-color:#C7843F !important}.gr-ects-f{border-left-color:#B0554B !important}
/* Plain editorial pages (CEFR, ECTS, EU student, education system, Lisbon,
 Schengen): one readable column, a real type scale and proper tables. */
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content{max-width:780px !important;margin-left:auto !important;margin-right:auto !important;padding-left:20px !important;padding-right:20px !important;color:#2B3A4F;font-size:16.5px;line-height:1.7}
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content h1{font-size:clamp(30px,3.6vw,44px) !important;line-height:1.12 !important;color:#12233D !important;margin:8px 0 18px !important}
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content h2{font-size:clamp(23px,2.4vw,29px) !important;line-height:1.2 !important;color:#12233D !important;margin:40px 0 12px !important}
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content h3{font-size:18px !important;font-weight:700 !important;color:#12233D !important;margin:28px 0 8px !important;font-family:inherit !important}
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content p{margin:0 0 16px}
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content ul,body.sie-prose-page .sie-content ol{margin:0 0 18px 1.2em;padding:0}
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content li{margin:0 0 6px}
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content a:not([class*="btn"]):not([class*="button"]){color:#0B5FA5;text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:3px;text-decoration-thickness:1px}
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content table{width:100% !important;border-collapse:collapse !important;margin:12px 0 28px !important;font-size:14.5px;background:#fff;border:1px solid #E4E0D8}
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content th{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important;text-align:left !important;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;font-weight:500;letter-spacing:1px;text-transform:uppercase;padding:10px 14px !important;border-bottom:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important}
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content td{padding:10px 14px !important;border-top:1px solid #EDEAE3 !important;vertical-align:top;color:#2B3A4F}
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content td{background:transparent !important}
body.sie-prose-page .sie-content td:first-child{color:#12233D !important;font-weight:700}
@media(max-width:640px){body.sie-prose-page .sie-content table{display:block;overflow-x:auto}}
/* ISCED progression bar: the narrower reading column clipped "Upper Secondary". */
body.sie-prose-page .isced-step{font-size:12px !important;line-height:1.3 !important}
/* "Ask Leonardo" banner used inside several guides (ECTS, Schengen…). */
.leonardo-banner{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;border:0 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}

 ~420px of enforced emptiness. Resetting the basis is the whole fix —
 never set flex-direction on an inherited flex container without checking
 what flex-basis meant before. */
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-text{flex:0 0 auto}
 .lh-hero .lh-portals--search{flex:0 0 auto}
 .lh-hero .lh-badge{margin-bottom:10px}
 .lh-hero .lh-title{margin:0 0 12px}
 .lh-hero .lh-subtitle{margin:0;max-width:52ch}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{position:relative;z-index:1;margin:clamp(14px,1.8vw,22px) 0 0;gap:10px 24px}
 /* The bar itself carries the emphasis: taller, larger type, and a navy
 action instead of the yellow one — yellow reads promotional, and on warm
 paper it was the loudest thing in the hero. Scoped to .lh-herosearch so
 the same widget elsewhere keeps the brand button. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-bar{min-height:64px;padding:4px 6px 4px 14px}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-input{font-size:17px}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-btn{background:#12233D;border-color:#12233D;color:#fff;font-weight:600}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-btn:hover{background:#1E3354;border-color:#1E3354}
 /* ── Results as a responsive grid, not a single strip ──────────────────
 .sie-res-list holds the program cards as direct children (verified live:
 18 cards, one parent, no headers in between), so one grid rule is enough.
 ⚠️ SCOPED TO THE HOMEPAGE ON PURPOSE. .sie-res-list is the shared
 SieFlowView markup — Leonardo renders into it too, with its own
 per-card animation offsets. Re-layouting it globally would change his
 results as a side effect of a homepage fix. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-res-list{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(320px,1fr));gap:16px;align-items:start}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-res-list > .program-card{width:auto;max-width:none;margin:0}
 /* The flow view (AI matching on) groups results into one .sie-flow__branch
 per country. Each branch carries max-width:560px inside a 798px rail, so
 two never fit and they stack — the "single strip". Releasing the cap and
 tiling the branches gives two country panels per row at this width, and
 more on a wider screen, without touching the cards inside.
 ⚠️ Scoped to .lh-herosearch: Leonardo renders the same flow markup. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-flow__branches{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(360px,1fr));gap:18px;align-items:start}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-flow__branch{max-width:none;width:100%}
 /* ── The figures strip ────────────────────────────────────────────────
 Serif numerals, monospaced labels, hairline rules, no card, no shadow,
 no colour fill behind each figure. The register of a register. */
 .lh-stats.lh-stats--figures{background:#F4F2ED;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-bottom:1px solid #E4E0D8;padding:0}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stats-grid{max-width:1200px;margin:0 auto;padding:0 clamp(16px,4vw,48px);display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,minmax(0,1fr));gap:0}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat{padding:clamp(20px,2.4vw,32px) clamp(14px,2vw,28px) clamp(20px,2.4vw,32px) 0;border-right:1px solid #E4E0D8;text-align:left;background:none;border-radius:0;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat:last-child{border-right:0}
 /* Every cell except the first gets inner space on its left, so each rule
 sits with equal air on both sides instead of crowding the next figure.
 The first keeps padding-left:0 so its numeral lines up with the margin
 the hero headline uses. */
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat + .lh-stat{padding-left:clamp(18px,2.4vw,34px)}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat-num{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:clamp(27px,2.9vw,40px);font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.5px;line-height:1.05;color:#12233D;background:none;-webkit-text-fill-color:currentColor}
 /* #6B7A8D measured 3.92:1 against the warm band — under the 4.5:1 that
 11.5px text needs. The cool grey was fine on the old cold background and
 quietly failed when the palette warmed up; #4F5967 measures 6.2:1.
 Worth remembering when warming any other background. */
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat-label{margin-top:8px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:1.3px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#4F5967}
 @media(max-width:700px){
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stats-grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat:nth-child(2){border-right:0}
 }
 /* Monogram instead of a repeated building glyph. Hairline tile, serif
 letters — it reads as a placeholder somebody chose, not as missing data. */
 .lh-uni-logo-placeholder{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;background:#F4F2ED;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:5px;color:#8A8578}
 .lh-uni-monogram{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:22px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:1px;color:#12233D}
 /* ── For institutions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
 The one full navy band on the page. It is dark on purpose: it marks a
 change of audience, so a student scrolling past knows at a glance that
 this part is not addressed to them. */
 .lh-inst{background:#12233D;color:#fff}
 .lh-inst-wrap *,.lh-inst-wrap *::before,.lh-inst-wrap *::after{box-sizing:border-box}
 .lh-inst-inner{max-width:1200px;margin:0 auto;padding:clamp(48px,6vw,88px) clamp(16px,4vw,48px);display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1.35fr) minmax(0,1fr);gap:clamp(28px,4vw,64px);align-items:start}
 .lh-inst-badge{margin:0 0 16px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:1.8px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-h{margin:0 0 16px;font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:clamp(26px,3.1vw,40px);line-height:1.16;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.5px;color:#fff;max-width:20ch}
 .lh-inst-body{margin:0 0 26px;font-size:clamp(15.5px,1.4vw,17px);line-height:1.65;color:#C6D2E0;max-width:54ch}
 .lh-inst-actions{margin:0;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:12px}
 .lh-inst-btn{display:inline-block;text-decoration:none;background:#fff;color:#12233D;font-size:15.5px;font-weight:600;padding:14px 26px;border:1px solid #fff;border-radius:4px;min-height:44px}
 .lh-inst-btn:hover{background:#F4F2ED;color:#12233D}
 .lh-inst-btn--ghost{background:none;color:#fff;border-color:#44597A;font-weight:500}
 .lh-inst-btn--ghost:hover{background:none;color:#fff;border-color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-terms{margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none}
 .lh-inst-terms li{border-top:1px solid #28405F;padding:20px 0}
 .lh-inst-terms li:first-child{border-top:0;padding-top:0}
 .lh-inst-k{margin:0 0 6px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:19px;color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-v{margin:0;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#C6D2E0}
 @media(max-width:860px){
 .lh-inst-inner{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 }
 @media(max-width:900px){
 .lh-hero .lh-portals--search{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-res-list{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-flow__branches{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 .lh-heroalt{flex-direction:row;flex-wrap:wrap}
 .lh-heroalt-card{flex:1 1 220px}
 .lh-hero-scrim{background:linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(250,248,244,.97) 0%,rgba(250,248,244,.93) 62%,rgba(250,248,244,.72) 100%)}
 }
 /* ── Institutional pass, part 2 (2026-11-08, evening) ──────────────────
 Brings the sections below the hero onto the palette and type the hero
 already uses, so the page reads as one document instead of two designs
 stacked on top of each other. Everything here is homepage-only (it lives
 in this template) and is pure CSS: delete this block to revert. */
 /* The page itself: the site-wide body is cold pale blue (#E8F1FA), which
 showed through every transparent section (the institutions carousel and
 the study fields block) as a blue band between warm ones. */
 body.page-id-150{background:#FAF8F4}
 /* ⚠️ THE HEADLINE NEVER WAS SERIF. leonardo-homepage-css.min.css carries
 `.lh-wrap .lh-title{font-family:system-ui !important; font-size:44px
 !important; font-weight:800 !important; color:#003b73 !important}`, so
 the Source Serif rule earlier in this block lost on every device. Only
 !important with equal-or-higher specificity can beat it. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-title,.lh-wrap .lh-hero h2.lh-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;font-size:clamp(34px,4.4vw,58px) !important;line-height:1.08 !important;letter-spacing:-.6px !important;color:#12233D !important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#12233D !important}
 /* The accent word: italic navy reads editorial; bright orange read promo. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-gradient-text{color:#12233D;-webkit-text-fill-color:#12233D;font-style:italic;font-weight:600}
 /* One label above the headline is enough. The H1 eyebrow ("STUDY IN
 EUROPE") already does that job; the extra pill only added noise. */
 .lh-hero .lh-badge{display:none}
 /* Phones: the hero had no side gutter, so the eyebrow sat flush against
 the screen edge while the centred text did not. Left-aligned, with the
 same 20px gutter as the rest of the page, it matches the desktop. */
 @media(max-width:900px){
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-center{padding-left:20px;padding-right:20px;box-sizing:border-box;text-align:left}
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-text,.lh-hero .lh-subtitle{text-align:left}
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-title{text-align:left}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{justify-content:flex-start}
 }
 /* ── Section headers: same voice as the institutions band ─────────────
 Serif headings and a small monospaced label instead of the rounded blue
 pills, which were the last "app" element on the page. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-header h2{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;font-size:clamp(28px,3vw,40px) !important;letter-spacing:-.4px;line-height:1.15;color:#12233D !important}
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-badge{display:inline-block;margin-bottom:14px;padding:0;background:none;border-radius:0;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;font-weight:500;letter-spacing:1.8px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#8C5A23}
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-sub{color:#4A525C}
 /* Section rhythm: paper / white / paper, so each block has an edge. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-how{background:#FAF8F4}
 .lh-wrap .lh-unis{background:#fff;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins{background:#fff;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8}
 /* How it works: the three steps were top-aligned, so the middle card
 (longer text) hung lower than its neighbours. Stretch evens them. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-steps{align-items:stretch}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step{background:#fff;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step-num{background:#12233D;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-weight:500}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step-icon{background:#F4F2ED;color:#12233D;border-radius:6px}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step-arrow{color:#B7B1A5}
 /* Cards: tighter corners and hairlines everywhere. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-card{border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins a[class*="card"],.lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins [class*="card"]{border-radius:6px;border-color:#E4E0D8;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--countries a[class*="card"],.lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--countries [class*="card"]{border-radius:6px}
 /* ── Study fields block (rendered by [sie_study_fields] after .lh-wrap) ─
 Six bright category colours, gradient pills and a gradient CTA made it
 the loudest part of the page. Same content, one navy, warm neutrals.
 The branch colours arrive as INLINE custom properties and inline
 backgrounds, so these overrides need !important to apply. Scoped to the
 homepage: the study-field pages keep their colour coding. */
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:clamp(28px,3vw,40px);letter-spacing:-.4px;color:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-subtitle{color:#4A525C}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__source-pill{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;box-shadow:none !important;border-radius:4px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__junction-dot{background:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch{--branch-color:#12233D !important;--branch-bg:#F4F2ED !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-accent{display:none}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-icon{background:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-count{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-card{background:#FAF8F4;border:1px solid #EDEAE3;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-card:hover{border-color:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-icon{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__leo-link{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-leonardo{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;border-radius:6px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-leo-btn{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border-color:#fff !important;border-radius:4px}
 /* Alignment: the search widget carries its own 24px side padding, so the
 bar sat indented from the headline above it; and the trust row was
 centred under a left-aligned column. Both now share the text's edge.
 Only the LEFT padding goes: removing the right one too pushed the
 "AI-enhanced matching" toggle across the seam into the navy side. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-wrap{padding-left:0 !important}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{justify-content:flex-start}
 /* Institution cards: the stylesheet tints each card top a different pastel
 (blue / yellow / blue) via !important rules at .lh-uni-card:nth-child()
 specificity, so this needs one more class to win. Plain paper, so the
 monogram or logo is the only thing that differs between cards. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-card:nth-child(n) .lh-uni-card-top{background:#F4F2ED !important;background-image:none !important;border-bottom:1px solid #EDEAE3}
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-cta{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
 .lh-wrap .sie-dest-hub__name{color:#12233D}
 /* Europe silhouette on the navy side. Present, never loud: a lighter blue
 at 15% so the copy on top keeps full contrast. The right edge fades out

 hairline seams between neighbouring countries; opacity sits on the <svg> itself so overlapping strokes cannot add up into darker lines. */

 DESTINATIONS PANEL  — overlay + grid
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
 /* Outer layer: covers full viewport */
 .sie-dest-panel {
 position: fixed;
 inset: 0;
 z-index: 2147483000;
 display: flex;
 align-items: stretch;
 justify-content: flex-end;
 opacity: 0;
 visibility: hidden;
 pointer-events: none;
 transition: opacity .25s ease, visibility .25s;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open {
 opacity: 1;
 visibility: visible;
 pointer-events: auto;
 }
 /* Backdrop */
 .sie-dest-panel__backdrop {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 background: rgba(11, 55, 112, .52);
 backdrop-filter: blur(3px);
 -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(3px);
 cursor: pointer;
 }
 /* Sheet — right-panel on desktop */
 .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 position: relative;
 z-index: 1;
 width: min(800px, 100%);
 height: 100%;
 background: #fff;
 overflow-y: auto;
 -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;
 padding: 26px 26px 40px;
 display: flex;
 flex-direction: column;
 gap: 0;
 transform: translateX(28px);
 opacity: 0;
 transition: transform .38s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), opacity .38s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1);
 box-shadow: -20px 0 48px rgba(0,0,0,.18);
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 transform: translateX(0);
 opacity: 1;
 }
 /* Mobile: bottom-sheet */
 @media (max-width: 767px) {
 .sie-dest-panel {
 align-items: flex-end;
 justify-content: stretch;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 width: 100%;
 height: 92vh;
 border-top-left-radius: 22px;
 border-top-right-radius: 22px;
 padding: 20px 16px 40px;
 transform: translateY(28px);
 box-shadow: 0 -16px 48px rgba(0,0,0,.18);
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 transform: translateY(0);
 }
 }
 /* ── Header ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__header {
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 justify-content: space-between;
 margin-bottom: 6px;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__titlewrap {
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 10px;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__globe {
 font-size: 22px;
 color: #1e66f5;
 line-height: 1;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__title {
 font-size: 1.5rem;
 font-weight: 800;
 color: #0b3770;
 margin: 0;
 line-height: 1.2;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__close {
 background: transparent;
 border: 0;
 font-size: 22px;
 color: #0b3770;
 cursor: pointer;
 padding: 6px 8px;
 border-radius: 8px;
 line-height: 1;
 opacity: .75;
 transition: opacity .15s, background .15s;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__close:hover {
 opacity: 1;
 background: #f0f4ff;
 }
 /* Subheading */
 .sie-dest-panel__sub {
 color: #466087;
 font-size: .94rem;
 margin: 0 0 20px;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 /* ── Country grid ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 display: grid;
 grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);
 gap: 14px;
 /* allow this to grow and scroll */
 flex: 1;
 align-content: start;
 }
 @media (max-width: 620px) {
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
 gap: 10px;
 }
 }
 @media (min-width: 621px) and (max-width: 860px) {
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
 }
 }
 /* ── Country card ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__card {
 position: relative;
 display: block;
 aspect-ratio: 3 / 2;
 border-radius: 12px;
 overflow: hidden;
 text-decoration: none;
 background: #1d3557;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card--no-img .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1d3557 0%, #1e66f5 100%);
 }
 /* Hero image layer — scales on hover */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 transition: transform .4s ease;
 will-change: transform;
 }
 /* <img> fills the card exactly like background-size:cover did.
 loading="lazy" means the browser only fetches each image when the
 panel opens and the card enters the viewport — saving ~30 MB of
 upfront image requests on every page that includes this panel. */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-img {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 width: 100%;
 height: 100%;
 object-fit: cover;
 object-position: center;
 display: block;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card:hover .sie-dest-panel__card-bg,
 .sie-dest-panel__card:focus-visible .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 transform: scale(1.07);
 }
 /* Gradient overlay + text */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-body {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 display: flex;
 flex-direction: column;
 justify-content: flex-end;
 padding: 10px 12px 10px;
 background: linear-gradient(
 to top,
 rgba(0, 0, 0, .72) 0%,
 rgba(0, 0, 0, .30) 55%,
 transparent 100%
 );
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card-name {
 color: #fff;
 font-weight: 700;
 font-size: .92rem;
 line-height: 1.2;
 text-shadow: 0 1px 5px rgba(0,0,0,.55);
 display: block;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow {
 display: block;
 color: rgba(255,255,255,0);
 font-size: .75rem;
 margin-top: 2px;
 transition: color .2s ease, transform .2s ease;
 line-height: 1;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card:hover .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow,
 .sie-dest-panel__card:focus-visible .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow {
 color: rgba(255,255,255,.9);
 transform: translateX(4px);
 }
 /* ── Body-scroll lock ── */
 body.sie-dest-panel-open {
 overflow: hidden;
 }
 /* ── Country interest heart ── */
 .sie-country-heart {
 position: absolute;
 top: 8px;
 right: 8px;
 z-index: 10;
 background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88);
 border: none;
 border-radius: 20px;
 padding: 4px 8px 4px 7px;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 4px;
 cursor: pointer;
 font-size: 13px;
 color: #94a3b8;
 box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.22);
 backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
 -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
 transition: color .18s, transform .18s, background .18s;
 line-height: 1;
 min-width: 28px;
 justify-content: center;
 }
 .sie-country-heart:hover {
 transform: scale(1.12);
 background: #fff;
 color: #ef4444;
 }
 .sie-country-heart.voted {
 color: #ef4444;
 background: #fff;
 }
 .sie-country-heart.voted i {
 animation: sie-heart-pop .35s cubic-bezier(.36,.07,.19,.97);
 }
 @keyframes sie-heart-pop {
 0%   { transform: scale(1); }
 40%  { transform: scale(1.45); }
 70%  { transform: scale(.88); }
 100% { transform: scale(1); }
 }
 .sie-country-heart__count {
 font-size: 11px;
 font-weight: 700;
 color: inherit;
 display: none;
 }
 .sie-country-heart.has-votes .sie-country-heart__count {
 display: inline;
 }
 /* ── Trigger button styles (for use in any menu) ── */
 /* Desktop globe icon */
 .se-dest-desktop-btn {
 font-size: 24px;
 color: #fff;
 text-decoration: none;
 cursor: pointer;
 transition: transform .2s, color .2s;
 position: relative;
 line-height: 1;
 background: transparent;
 border: 0;
 padding: 0;
 }
 .se-dest-desktop-btn:hover {
 transform: scale(1.15);
 color: #FFCC00;
 }
 /* Tooltip on desktop */
 @media (min-width: 1024px) {
 .se-dest-desktop-btn::after {
 content: "Study Destinations";
 position: absolute;
 bottom: -30px;
 left: 50%;
 transform: translateX(-50%);
 background: #007BFF;
 color: #fff;
 padding: 4px 8px;
 font-size: 12px;
 border-radius: 5px;
 opacity: 0;
 pointer-events: none;
 transition: opacity .2s;
 white-space: nowrap;
 }
 .se-dest-desktop-btn:hover::after {
 opacity: 1;
 }
 }
 /* Mobile pill button */
 .se-dest-btn {
 background: #0b3770 !important;
 color: #fff !important;
 }
 .se-dest-btn:hover {
 background: #1e66f5 !important;

  <title>Conference on the Future of Europe : the future is in your hands</title>
  <link>https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/whats-new/news/conference-on-the-future-of-europe-the-future-is-in-your-hands</link>
  <description>
<h1 class="title-h1 eac-page-title">Conference on the Future of Europe : the future is in your hands</h1>
<span><span>sandoel</span></span>
<span><time datetime="2021-12-07T08:55:30+01:00" title="Tuesday, December 7, 2021 - 08:55">Tue, 12/07/2021 - 08:55</time>
</span>
<div class="ecl"><h2><strong>What is the Conference?</strong></h2>

<p>The <strong>Conference on the Future of Europe </strong>is the first transnational discussion with Europeans on how to address Europe’s challenges together. This is an opportunity to think about what citizens and&nbsp; civil society want for the European Union.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>
</div>

  </article>

                                                                <div class="video-description lc-stripe-wrapper-text"><div><p>The European Parliament, the Council, and the European Commission have committed to listen and follow up on the recommendations made</p></div></div>

<div class="lc-padding-top-half lc-padding-bottom-default lc-background-color-white lc-contained eac-stripe eac-stripe--bg-white" id="paragraph-827">  <div class="eac-stripe__inner">            <div class="full-html-body">
  <div class="eac-body lc-stripe-wrapper-text"><h2><strong>How does the Conference work?</strong></h2>

<p>Europeans can share ideas via the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/?locale=en" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Multilingual Digital Platform</a>, and both national and&nbsp;<a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/assemblies/citizens-panels" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">European Citizens' Panels</a>. These contributions feed into the&nbsp;<a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/pages/plenary" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Conference Plenaries</a>.</p>

<p>The Conference&nbsp;offers a new public forum for an open, inclusive, and transparent debate with citizens around a number of key priorities and challenges.</p>

<h2><strong>How can you participate?</strong></h2>

<ul>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]--><a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/processes?locale=en&amp;pk_source=pdf_document&amp;pk_medium=link&amp;pk_campaign=europarl" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">share your own ideas or support others’ ideas</a> on the multilingual digital Conference platform</li>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]-->organise your own events and promote it by adding them to the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/?locale=en&amp;pk_source=pdf_document&amp;pk_medium=link&amp;pk_campaign=europarl" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Conference platform</a></li>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]-->take a look at the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/meetings" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">events organised by people across the EU</a></li>
</ul>

<h2><strong>What will the outcome be?</strong></h2>

<p>All of the ideas gathered and reports on events are published on the platform openly and transparently. These reports will then directly influence the discussions in the European Citizens’ Panels as well as in the Plenaries, where citizens will enter into a dialogue with national and European decision makers.</p>

<p>By spring 2022, the Conference will provide guidance on the future of Europe to the European institutions</p>

<p><a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/pages/getinvolved" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Get involved and make your voice heard when it comes to education, culture, youth, sport, and more</a>.</p>

<p>Follow on Twitter at&nbsp;</p>

<ul>

</ul>

WHO WE ARE<\/strong> <\/p>

Proxima Fusion is Europe\u2019s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent\u2019s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over \u20ac650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world\u2019s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.<\/p>

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.<\/p>

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/div>

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION<\/strong><\/p>

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.<\/p><\/li>

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.<\/p><\/li>

  • Do your life\u2019s best work and enjoy the journey.<\/p><\/li>

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

    \u00a0<\/div>

    YOUR IMPACT<\/strong><\/p>

    At Proxima Fusion, we're developing the world's leading stellarator technology. To turn cutting-edge designs into reality, we need skilled technicians who can bring complex, first-of-a-kind hardware to life. As a Technician at Proxima Fusion, you'll work hands-on with Proxima-designed components, magnets, mechanical assemblies and other critical systems, supporting their build, assembly, integration and testing.<\/p>

    Working closely with Engineering, Manufacturing and Quality, you'll help turn ambitious designs into reliable hardware, solve practical challenges on the shop floor and contribute to developing the processes and tooling needed to build Alpha. This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced engineering and hands-on manufacturing, helping build one of Europe's most ambitious engineering projects.<\/p>

    \u00a0<\/div>

    WHAT YOU WILL DO<\/strong><\/p>

    • Build, assemble and modify prototypes, experimental hardware, custom tooling and development rigs for engineering and special projects across the programme.<\/p><\/li>

    • Turn engineering drawings, models, and sketches into practical hardware. Clarify missing requirements and agree the build approach with the responsible engineer before committing to uncertain or irreversible steps.<\/p><\/li>

    • Fabricate and adapt components using fitting, cutting, drilling, soldering, bonding and assembly techniques within your competence. Coordinate specialist machining, welding or other work when needed.<\/p><\/li>

    • Identify buildability issues early, including tolerance stacks, inaccessible fasteners, component fit and assembly sequence, and provide practical feedback to the design team.<\/p><\/li>

    • Prepare and run development trials, including winding, joining, insulation and impregnation trials as assigned. Install instrumentation, commission rigs with engineers, take measurements and record what changed and what happened.<\/p><\/li>

    • Investigate unexpected behaviour, propose practical fixes and work through build-test-modify iterations with engineers.<\/p><\/li>

    • Organise the practical delivery of assigned projects: source small parts and consumables through agreed purchasing routes, arrange tools and build activities, and keep the workshop ready for use. Communicate progress, blockers and changing priorities to the lead technician.<\/p><\/li>

    • Keep clear as-built records, annotated drawings, photographs, settings and trial observations so another technician can reproduce the work and understand each modification.<\/p><\/li>

    • Transfer proven prototypes and methods to manufacturing or routine testing through initial work instructions, tooling, assembly sequences, training and technical handovers.<\/p><\/li>

    • Work with engineers to identify hazards and establish the necessary risk assessments and controls before starting work on unproven hardware.<\/p>

      \u00a0<\/div><\/li><\/ul>

      WHO YOU ARE<\/strong><\/p>

      • A technical apprenticeship or vocational qualification in mechanical, electrical, mechatronic or related engineering work, or equivalent hands-on experience.<\/p><\/li>

      • Hands-on experience building, modifying and troubleshooting mechanical or electromechanical hardware in a workshop, laboratory, development or advanced manufacturing environment.<\/p><\/li>

      • The ability to interpret engineering drawings, tolerances and 3D models, with working familiarity with geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) and practical measurement skills.<\/p><\/li>

      • Confident hand-tool and workshop skills, sound fabrication and assembly judgement, and a willingness to develop unfamiliar techniques.<\/p><\/li>

      • Resourcefulness with incomplete information: you investigate, ask useful questions, find suitable parts and propose a practical next step while keeping the engineering objective clear.<\/p><\/li>

      • Sound judgement about technical uncertainty, safety and when a build or design change requires engineering review before proceeding.<\/p><\/li>

      • The ability to organise work, adapt to agreed priority changes and document configurations and findings clearly.<\/p><\/li>

      • Working English for technical discussions, drawings, instructions and build records.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

        Nice to have<\/h3>

        • Specialist fabrication skills such as manual or CNC machining, sheet-metal work, welding, brazing or additive manufacturing.<\/p><\/li>

        • Experience creating or modifying simple parts and fixtures in CATIA, SolidWorks, Fusion 360 or similar CAD tools.<\/p><\/li>

        • Experience with instrumentation, sensors, data acquisition, electrical wiring, vacuum, cryogenics or superconducting hardware.<\/p><\/li>

        • Experience with composites, resins, vacuum bagging, insulation or impregnation.<\/p><\/li>

        • Experience taking first-of-a-kind hardware or a prototype process through to repeatable manufacturing and technical handover.<\/p><\/li>

        • German language skills.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

          INTERVIEW PROCESS<\/strong><\/p>

          • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)<\/p><\/li>

          • Technical Screening (30 min)<\/p><\/li>

          • Technical Panel (3x60 min)<\/p><\/li>

          • CEO call (30 min)<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.


Please make your application, including your CV, in English Language. We are a global compliance team headquartered out of London.

About the role

As a Senior Analyst – Permanent Controls, you will join the Permanent Controls team, a global Second Line of Defence (2LoD) function based across Paris and Mauritius. Reporting directly to the Head of Permanent Controls within the Compliance department, you will focus on the financial perimeter, exercising second-line control, independent oversight, and framework monitoring over the organization's finance domain. You will partner closely with the First Line of Defence (1LoD) to establish control standards, design control matrices, and provide guidance when needed. You will also execute 2LoD control plans, issue formal findings, and track recommendations through to resolution.

 

Sitting in the Second Line of Defense, the global Permanent Controls team serves as an ongoing, trusted advisor and objective challenge to operational teams (1LoD), helping them design robust controls and ensure operational integrity across the organization.

Unlike periodic audit functions, Permanent Controls operates continuously to proactively identify vulnerabilities, standardize control frameworks, and foster a strong risk culture.

 

Note on Governance: This is a 2LoD function focused on ongoing control design, execution, and 1LoD enablement. It is distinct and independent from the Internal Audit (3LoD) function within Checkout.com.

 

Key responsibilities

  • Control Design: Collaborate with stakeholders to translate identified risks into comprehensive 2nd line control plans, standards, and templates.

  • 1LoD Enablement: Partner with the First Line of Defence teams to design, refine, and assess their control matrices, ensuring alignment with internal standards and regulators' expectations (ACPR, FCA..).

  • Execution & Testing: Formalize and execute second line permanent controls across critical perimeters, including:

    • Financial regulatory reporting across global entities (France, UK, US, etc.).

    • Accuracy of financial data, accounting standards, and reconciliations.

    • Internal financial processes, procedures, and statutory compliance (including the Order of 3 December 2014).

    • Safeguarding mechanisms (flow of funds, compliance with safeguarding measures, timelines, and incident monitoring).

  • Reporting & Escalation: Present detailed control findings and anomaly reports to the Head of Permanent Controls; track the implementation of remediation recommendations.

  • Proactive Continuous Improvement: Identify operational control gaps, take the initiative to propose practical solutions, and drive improvements to the overall control framework.

  • Tooling & Automation: Contribute to the implementation and optimization of automated control tools, tracking dashboards, and recommendation monitoring systems whenever possible.

 

About You

  • Experience: 5 years of experience in Financial Audit, Internal Control, or Financial Reporting within the financial services (banking, Fintech..) or payments industry.

  • Regulatory Context: Familiarity with regulatory frameworks and ACPR expectations is strongly preferred.

  • Mindset & Working Style:

    • Proactive & Autonomous: A "go-getter" who takes ownership, anticipates control gaps, and brings actionable solutions to the table rather than waiting for direction.

    • Naturally Curious: A drive to understand end-to-end business operations, data flows, and complex payment mechanics.

    • Rigorous & Analytical: Meticulous attention to detail with an ability to leverage data analytics to evaluate controls, transactions and processes objectively.

  • Languages: Fluency in French and English is required.

  • Communication: Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to communicate clear findings and influence decision-making across lines of defence.

Bring all of you to work

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

Life at Checkout.com

We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the Role

As an Account Development Representative (ADR) at Samsara, you will be trained, both on the job and with formal training programs led by a world-class team of sales professionals, to take on your next role as closing Account Executive. 

On a daily basis, you will be responsible for sourcing pipelines for our EMEA business,  generating opportunities via outbound outreach. 

We have offices in Munich, Paris and Amsterdam and we offer remote working from Germany, France, The Netherlands and London. Our European headquarters are based in London.

This is a remote position open to candidates based in France, Germany, The Netherlands and United Kingdom. This position requires working hours in CEST. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

You should apply if: 

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. Successful ADRs can see promotion to a closing role in two years or less.
  • You love talking to people: In this role, you will average 60+ calls to prospective customers daily.
  • You have an innate curiosity about how businesses work: One day you'll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support to make a larger impact.
  • You treat rejection as a learning experience: In this role, you will get hung up on and you will get told no. You need to have the resilience to pick up the phone again and again to sell Samsara's mission.
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara's high-performance Sales culture means you'll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

In this role, you will: 

  • Drive pipeline through personalized outreach to prospects via phone, emails and Linkedin
  • Have the opportunity to to participate in trade/shows events to represent the Samsara brand and connect with prospective customers and partners.
  • Become a product expert and learn the Samsara way of selling
  • Keep meticulous records of interactions with accounts in our CRM (Salesforce.com)
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 1-3 years professional experience, ideally in customer facing roles
  • 6-12 months sales experience as a minimum
  • Highly motivated and committed, with strong desire to work in target driven sales
  • Proven track record of consistent over achievement of targets/expectations of previous roles
  • Excellent communication skills, verbal and written
  • Curious and able to ask insightful questions
  • A champion of a Growth Mindset
  • Highly proficient in English and fluent in French

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience in closing-sales roles
  • Proven track record of achievements beyond work (e.g. academics, sports, charity, …)
  • Willingness to collaborate and influence in a "win as a team" environment
  • Excitement about solving new problems in innovative ways
